card.name: Digits inside chemical and PK terms
card.fires_on: A single digit (0, 2, 5) that sits inside a technical term and is followed by a hyphen or letter. Examples are the 0 in AUC 0-inf, the 5 in D5W, and the 5 in uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase.

modes.label: AUC subscript
modes.description: The 0 after AUC before a range such as -INF or -12.
modes.example: increased S- and R- verapamil AUC <<0>>-12 by 36%

modes.label: D5W solution name
modes.description: The 5 inside D5W, the dextrose 5% in water diluent.
modes.example: 6 mg/mL NS or D<<5>>W 24 hours 7 days

modes.label: Chemical name locant
modes.description: A position number inside a chemical name, such as 5' in uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyl or 2 in 2-ethylhexyl.
modes.example: Phenobarbital increases L-thyroxine metabolism by inducing uridine <<5>>’-diphospho-gluc

card.writes: It seems to prepare a hyphenated continuation, such as a -letter or -dimensional style compound, after a digit.
card.plain: It fires on a lone number buried inside a technical term, like the 0 in AUC 0-inf or the 5 in D5W.
